For instance, golf novelty products or golf 
gifts or golf gifts for men. That's a way of

niching down your product, so it applies to less 
people, but you can better serve that targeted

market rather than just generic hats or golf 
tees. Similarly, Travis noticed that no one was

serving the electrolyte market and targeting the 
carnivore diet on Amazon. So, he stood up a brand

that specifically targeted those on the carnivore 
diet that were in need of electrolytes. The next

reason why people may be hesitant to start 
and brand on Amazon is due to startup costs.

Creating your own passion product on Amazon 
will have some startup costs that are going

to be higher than some of the other methods of 
selling on Amazon like retail arbitrage. However,

spending this extra money up front is going to 
yield dividends for the future. Because while

methods like retail arbitrage constantly force 
you to find new products and list them on Amazon,

creating your own passion product, you can list 
that product and create a family of products that

continue to sell passively in perpetuity. So 
as soon as you create the brand architecture,

you can just keep making money and making money 
because you're the only one selling the products

that you're making. Startup costs for a new Amazon 
business when you're creating a Prashion product

include things like creating an LLC or a DBA, 
getting a trademark registered, creating a logo,

creating a custom design and possibly a custom 
product, getting samples of that product in

addition to doing an initial manufacturing run. 
Depending on the type of product you're creating,

this can cost anywhere from two to upwards of 
$10,000 or more. However, there are ways to ensure

you do it in the most efficient manner possible, 
and Travis talks about all of them in his passion

product formula course. There are ways to limit or 
minimize almost all of the startup costs you have

by crowdfunding the campaign through Kickstarter 
or other crowdfunding channels. This will enable

you to raise money before you start selling. 
With crowdfunding, concern is really low because

if your Kickstarter fails to get funded, then 
you don't have to move forward with the idea.

However, if many people think it's a great 
idea and fund your Kickstarter campaign,

only then do you have to move forward 
with creating the product. I made around

$4,000 on Kickstarter for my Bogeys and Beers 
campaign before I started making the products.

The fourth reason people do not start their Amazon 
business is because of fear of recession. Every

year people are concerned about a recession, but 
Amazon is getting more and more profitable every

year. During 2020, data shows that people cut back 
on expenses like vacations, but they continued to

spend money on e-commerce retail even during COVID 
and perhaps especially during COVID. For example,

products that are necessities have a higher 
chance of being recession proof. For example,

pet supplies, baby products, and groceries sell 
really well during a recession or not. And because

people couldn't go on vacation during COVID, even 
though it might have been considered a recession,

they were still spending money on small 
premium retail products on Amazon. However,

if you think about it, something like retail 
arbitrage is not recession proof. And if a

recession were to occur, that would be a big 
concern. So don't let fear hold you back. In fact,

many of the most successful Fortune 500 companies 
were started during a recession. And this brings

me to the final point about why people are 
afraid of starting a business on Amazon in 2025,

and that is increasing fees. Honestly, when I 
was thinking about starting to sell my product

on Amazon, I too was concerned about increasing 
fees on Amazon. Pick, pack, and ship fees were

on the rise. However, Amazon's 15% fee that they 
charge every seller for every unit that's sold

on the website did not and has not gone up. In 
addition, Amazon has promised not to raise fees

in 2025. Increased fees are always a risk when 
starting a business with a company like Amazon.

The amount of time, effort, and energy you save 
by having them take care of the marketing and

distribution of your product more than offsets 
the fees that they charge right now. So, the

opportunity is still great to make a lot of money. 
You just need to make sure you choose a product

with high enough margins to offset small increases 
in fees that are likely to come. For example,

there's the product cost plus Amazon's 15% fee 
to sell on their platform for every unit sold,

plus the Amazon pick, pack, and ship FBA fee. Not 
to mention the marketing fees for PPC, which is

Amazon pay per click, where you can pay a certain 
amount of money per click to show up at the top

of search results. Now, all of these fees may 
seem like a lot of money, and they are. However,

no matter how you sell your product, you're still 
going to have to pay to ship it to your customers.

You're still going to have to pay for customer 
service, and you're still going to have to pay

marketing to drive leads so people can find and 
buy your product. So, even with all of the fees,

these are things that you're going to have to pay 
for anyways, and it takes a huge load off you not

to handle customer service and distribution and 
marketing. So you can just focus on making the

best product possible and just be sure to give 
yourself enough margins to account for these fees

and still be profitable. The problem with some of 
these other selling methods like private label is

if other people come into the marketplace and 
start selling the exact same thing that you're

selling with a different label, you're going 
to be caught in a price war to the bottom and

you're going to be forced to lower your price to 
sell these items. and that's going to lower your

profit margin. However, with a passion product, 
you can position yourself as a premium product,

which will enable you to preserve those margins 
and not get caught up in a race to the bottom.

Selling generic products means when other sellers 
lower their price, you cannot raise your price or

even keep it the same and keep those customers. 
But with passion products, that is not a big

concern of mine. These products have higher profit 
margins and customers buying premium products are

less price sensitive. For instance, my Bogeys
and Beers golf hat is made of the finest quality

material. It's 95% polyester, 5% spandex. It's 
actually the same blend as the Melin hats use,

and those hats are selling for $70. My hats are 
selling for $34.99 on Amazon. Still higher than

many other hats on Amazon. However, I'm 
using a premium quality material. I have

premium branding which enables me to sell for 
higher than other hats. And believe me, if you

try and do retail arbitrage or private labeling, 
you will not be able to have these margins. So,

even if Amazon raises fees in 2025 or beyond, 
I have the price ability to raise my prices and

not lose my customers as easily as someone 
who's doing retail arbitrage and selling a

generic product. Bogeys and Beers customers are 
going to get a great deal no matter what. The

Melin Hats are using the same quality material 
and they're selling for double the price. So,

we're always going to have great pricing at 
Bogeys and Beers. We're always going to use

better quality material and that's what's going to 
enable us to stay competitive and keep our profit

margins because we're creating so much value for 
our customers. Because we put that money and time

and effort into design and material quality on the 
front end, it enables us not to have to do that

on the back end. So, in conclusion, creating 
your own passion product is a far better way

to make money on Amazon than private label, than 
retail arbitrage, and then wholesale. If you want

to learn how to start your own Amazon business, 
I recommend joining Travis's Amazon FBA course,

The Passion Product Formula. It has over 
100 tutorials on every step in the process

of creating your Amazon business, one-on-one 
coaching sessions, and my personal favorite,

live Q&As's with an experienced Amazon seller 
who's proven themselves as a competent Amazon

seller who can answer any questions you might 
have throughout the process. Click the link in the

description below to sign up for the weight list 
now. But if you're not ready to join just yet,

Travis does have a completely free 10-hour Amazon 
FBA course. And you can get it by clicking the

link here. And if you want to check out my Bogeys
and Beers products, my Bogeys and Beers hat or my

Bogeys and Beers golf tea based drinking games 
with jokes, challenge, and drinking actions

on each and every tea. Click the link in the 
description and you can go to my Amazon website

19th hole golf or type in Bogeys and Beers on Amazon. 
And good luck to you on your Amazon journey.
